correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and each fixed position i, deleting and standardizing yields a uniform permutation of size n-1. Only the inserted fixed point can add a record, precisely when the earlier entries are the i-1 smaller labels. This gives the exact polynomial. Adjacent polynomial products differ by (n-2i) times a rising-product with nonnegative coefficients, proving all upper-tail comparisons by a telescoping coefficient identity. Real nonpositive roots imply unimodal coefficients, giving exact total variation; summing tails gives exact W1. The expected counts and fixed-point covariance follow by differentiation. The independent exact verifier checks all permutations to n=9 and polynomial laws through n=80, but the proof is all-size.

originality.rationale: The classical one-variable record polynomial and ordinary fixed-point counts are explicitly prior. The novel candidate is the exact all-threshold stochastic order as the conditioned fixed position moves toward the center, and the sharp adjacent Wasserstein and total-variation laws. The original primary works examined address fixed-point adjacency statistics, coherent record-conditioned measures, mesh-pattern statistics, and strong fixed-point/record joint counts. None inspected establishes or directly implies the position-specific stochastic ladder; the proof includes a new structured cancellation of adjacent conditioning polynomials. Search noncoverage is not proof of worldwide priority, so residual historical risk is stated.
residual_risks: Bounded literature and semantic-database retrieval cannot establish that no older paper gives an equivalent result in different notation.
A sufficiently detailed, uninspected extension of a mesh-pattern or record/fixedpoint joint generating-function framework might cover this statement implicitly.
Selected baseline is an August 2013 Berkeley technical report; its early public listing, rather than any later journal issue, is used for dating.

value.rationale: Position-indexed fixed-point conditioning is a canonical finite-probability question. The result ranks full conditional distributions simultaneously at all thresholds and provides precise transport and total-variation magnitudes. It also identifies a systematic endpoint-to-center dependency inversion, which a single mean/covariance cannot capture. This is a structural comparative law with general n and explicit equality and sign boundaries, not merely a renamed classical record identity.
